article_content: Linda Cooper, a 60-year member of Ridgedale Church of Christ in Collegedale, Tennessee, was expelled after refusing to denounce her daughter Kat's same-sex marriage. Church elders issued a Sunday ultimatum: publicly repent or leave. Linda and two siblings chose departure. The expulsion followed Kat Cooper's successful campaign as a Collegedale police detective to secure health benefits for spouse Krista. This August 5 policy change made Collegedale Tennessee's first city with same-sex partner benefits, attracting statewide media attention. Linda's visible support - including attending key meetings and embracing Kat after the 4-1 City Council vote - conflicted with church doctrine. Kat stated: 'They're exiling members for loving their children unconditionally.' Hunt Cooper described his wife's distress: 'She's traumatized. It's like losing family.' The Coopers' deep church ties intensify the pain - Linda's father was a former elder, and Kat grew up maintaining church facilities. Minister Ken Willis acknowledged mixed reactions but declined elaboration, calling it 'an in-church private issue.' The case underscores tensions between social progress and religious traditions.

article_content: An alleged North Korean propaganda video circulating online makes extraordinary claims about American life, including that citizens drink 'hot snow' as coffee, reside in tents, and consume wild birds weekly. The four-minute production portrays the U.S. as a nation in severe decline, with narration suggesting Americans sleep on floors and rely on North Korean aid. While presented as official propaganda, analysts question the video's authenticity, suggesting it may be satire mimicking Pyongyang's style. The film incorporates global disaster footage, including scenes from Paris' Gare du Nord station, to support its narrative of American hardship. Among its more bizarre assertions: Americans allegedly hunt birds to near-extinction, reserving remaining 'yummy birds' for Tuesday meals. The video also claims former political figures beg for 'snow coffee' and shows individuals surrounded by body bags containing deceased companions. The release coincides with reports of North Korean food shortages and follows recent state media images of Kim Jong Un inspecting fish farms. Experts suggest such propaganda aims to deflect from domestic challenges while reinforcing anti-American sentiment.

Den fire minutter lange video skildrer USA som en nation i kraftig nedgang, hvor amerikanere ifølge fortælleren sover på gulve og er afhængige af nordkoreansk bistand. Selvom videoen præsenteres som officiel propaganda, betvivler analytikere dens ægthed og mener den kan være satire inspireret af Pyongyangs stil. Filmen bruger optagelser fra globale katastrofer, herunder scener fra Paris' Gare du Nord, til at underbygge sin fortælling om amerikanske vanskeligheder. Blandt de mere bizarre påstande er, at amerikanere angiveligt har jaget fugle til nær udryddelse og spiser de sidste 'lækre fugle' hver tirsdag. Videoen hævder også, at tidligere politikere tigger om 'snekaffe' og viser personer omgivet af ligposer med afdøde kammerater. Udgivelsen følger rapporter om madmangel i Nordkorea og nylige statsmedie-billeder af Kim Jong Un, der inspicerer fiskefarme. Eksperter hævder, at sådan propaganda forsøger at fjerne fokus fra indenlandske problemer samtidig med at den styrker anti-amerikanske holdninger.

article_content: Residents of Cumbria and North Yorkshire witnessed a rare Northern Lights display, typically seen near the Arctic Circle. Photographer Owen Humphreys captured the aurora borealis near Dunstanburgh Castle on a moonless night, describing it as 'the best show in years.' The phenomenon occurs when charged solar particles collide with Earth's atmosphere, exciting oxygen molecules (creating green/yellow hues at 96km altitude) and nitrogen (producing blue/red colors at 321km). Kielder Observatory confirmed it was the strongest display in recent memory. While usually visible near polar regions, clear skies and minimal light pollution allowed UK sightings. Google Street View recently added Northern Lights imagery from Finland, enabling virtual exploration of this atmospheric marvel through 360-degree panoramas.

Fænomenet opstår, når ladede solpartikler kolliderer med Jordens atmosfære og får iltmolekyler til at lyse grønt/gult i 96 km højde, mens nitrogen skaber blå/røde farver ved 321 km. Kielder Observatory bekræftede, at det var den stærkeste manifestation i nyere tid. Klart vejr og minimal lysforurening muliggjorde sjældne observationer i Storbritannien. Google Street View har tilføjet nordlysbilleder fra Finland, så alle nu kan opleve dette natursyn virtuelt gennem 360-graders panoramaer.

article_content: Police investigating Madeleine McCann's disappearance have identified a suspect linked to multiple child sexual assaults at Algarve resorts between 2004 and 2006. Detectives report 12 break-ins at holiday homes, including five assaults on British girls aged 7 to 10. Three cases were reported following renewed appeals in October 2022. The suspect, described as tanned with dark hair and speaking English with a foreign accent, targeted properties in Praia da Luz, Carvoeiro, and Vale da Parra. Distinctive clothing included a burgundy long-sleeve top with a white circle. DCI Andy Redwood stated the pattern reveals 'an unhealthy interest in young white female children.' Portuguese authorities initially dismissed connections due to the incidents' geographic spread. The current investigation includes 38 persons of interest and reviews of 530 sex offenders, with 59 classified as high priority. International cooperation continues, though officials express frustration with legal process delays.

article_content: The White House has confirmed President Barack Obama will maintain Joe Biden as his running mate for the 2012 election, dismissing Republican suggestions to replace him with Hillary Clinton. This follows controversy over Biden's August 13 remarks in Danville, Virginia, where he told an African American audience that Republican policies would 'put y'all back in chains' through financial deregulation. White House Press Secretary Jay Carney stated on August 16: 'The vice-presidential selection was settled long ago. While we respect Senator McCain, we wouldn't seek his advice on running mates.' Obama and Biden held scheduled meetings at the White House, including a joint session with Secretary of State Clinton, amid intensified scrutiny of their working relationship. In interviews with People magazine and Entertainment Tonight, Obama acknowledged Biden's phrasing as 'a distraction' but praised his commitment to middle-class issues. Political analysts consider a Biden replacement before the September Democratic National Convention in Charlotte improbable, noting such a move would signal campaign instability. Clinton's potential 2016 presidential bid further reduces likelihood of her accepting vice-presidential nomination. Biden's speech to 800 attendees at the Institute for Advanced Learning and Research continues to dominate political discourse, with Republicans condemning the rhetoric while Democrats emphasize the substantive debate about Wall Street regulation.

Hvide Husets pressechef Jay Carney udtalte den 16. august: 'Valget af vicepræsidentkandidat blev afgjort for længst. Selvom vi respekterer senator McCain, ville vi ikke søge hans råd om vicepræsidentkandidater.' Obama og Biden gennemførte planlagte møder i Det Hvide Hus, herunder et fælles møde med udenrigsminister Clinton, under intens granskning af deres samarbejde. Politiske analytikere vurderer det usandsynligt, at Biden bliver erstattet før Demokratikonventet i Charlotte i september, da sådant skridt ville signalere ustabilitet. Clintons mulige præsidentkandidatur i 2016 gør det yderligere usandsynligt, at hun vil acceptere vicepræsidentposten. Bidens tale til 800 tilhørere på Institute for Advanced Learning and Research dominerer fortsat den politiske debat, hvor republikanere fordømmer retorikken, mens demokrater fremhæver den substansielle diskussion om regulering af Wall Street.

article_content: (CNN) Investigators examining the Malaysia Airlines crash in Ukraine face multiple unprecedented challenges, including restricted access to the debris field and ongoing militant activity. The downing of Flight MH17 with 298 people aboard has raised critical questions about the investigation's leadership and process. Aviation experts emphasize the need for an impartial inquiry excluding parties involved in the Ukraine-Russia conflict. Ukrainian President Petro Poroshenko confirmed participation from the UN's International Civil Aviation Organization alongside Dutch, Malaysian, and US representatives. Malaysian Prime Minister Najib Razak demanded full international access to the crash site. Recovery of the aircraft's black boxes remains crucial but complicated by the volatile region, according to CNN analysts Richard Quest and Miles O'Brien. 'The critical issue is ensuring objective international analysis of the flight recorders,' O'Brien noted. While US and Ukrainian officials allege a surface-to-air missile strike using a Buk system, Russia denies involvement. Malaysian authorities refrain from definitive conclusions as conflicting narratives emerge. Ukrainian security chief Valentyn Nalyvaichenko claims intercepted communications implicate Russian intelligence officers, vowing accountability. Former US intelligence official Philip Mudd suggests technical surveillance will clarify the missile's origin. US radar data reportedly detected missile launch signatures coinciding with the crash. Forensic analysis of the debris pattern – showing wide dispersion characteristic of mid-air breakup – supports missile strike hypotheses. Separatist control of the crash site hampers investigation efforts, with verified reports of evidence tampering. CNN's Nic Robertson documented five-hour delays in securing the area and armed interference with rescue operations. While US agencies prepare to assist through NTSB and FBI teams in advisory roles, access remains uncertain in rebel-held territory. Satellite imagery analysis and State Department diplomacy aim to identify the launch location and support victims' families.

article_content: A new form of digital theft has emerged in public spaces, with criminals using RFID technology to steal payment card details without physical contact. Security expert David Bryan from Chicago's Trustwave demonstrated how portable RFID readers can capture card information from up to 15cm away. This 'digital skimming' exploits contactless payment technology found in 70% of credit cards. Protective solutions include foil-lined wallets and mobile payment systems like Apple Pay. Chase Bank plans to phase out RFID cards, while products like Articulate's $35 clutch purse (developed by San Diego-based entrepreneurs) aim to block RFID signals. Experts emphasize the need for improved security measures as RFID readers become increasingly accessible.

Sikkerhedsekspert David Bryan fra Trustwave i Chicago demonstrerede, hvordan bærbare RFID-læsere kan opsnappe kortinformation fra op til 15 cm afstand. Denne 'digitale skimming' udnytter kontaktløs betalingsteknologi, som findes i 70% af kreditkort. Beskyttelsestiltag inkluderer folieforede tegnebøger og mobilbetalingsløsninger som Apple Pay. Chase Bank planlægger at fase ud RFID-kort, mens produkter som Articulates 35$ clutchtaske (fra San Diego-baserede iværksættere) skal blokere RFID-signaler. Eksperter kræver bedre sikkerhedsforanstaltninger, da RFID-udstyr bliver lettere tilgængeligt.

Built primarily from recycled driftwood and builders' scrap, it offers five-star comforts such as Egyptian cotton linens and designer bathrobes. The project, inspired by a child's request during a cabin stay, overcame initial local objections to become a successful holiday let with perfect TripAdvisor ratings and international bookings.

article_content: (CNN) -- Remember Wikipedia's black banner donation requests? Expect more campaigns to keep the non-profit encyclopedia ad-free. 'Maintaining independence is crucial. We prefer staying advertisement-free,' co-founder Jimmy Wales told CNN's Richard Quest. The platform successfully raised $16 million from 500,000 donors during its 2010 fundraising drive, according to Wikimedia Foundation records. While critics might view these campaigns as digital panhandling, Wales stresses avoiding conflicts: 'Imagine reading about General Motors with a Corvette ad nearby.' The entrepreneur clarifies he's not anti-advertising overall – he runs for-profit Wikia, hosting over 200,000 community-built gaming and entertainment wikis. Wales compares Wikipedia to 'a temple for the mind' maintained by global volunteers making over 1.7 billion edits. 'It's seemingly impossible, yet it works through humanity's collaborative spirit,' he remarked about the crowdsourced model.

Ifølge Wikimedia Foundation nåede platformen at indsamle 16 millioner dollars fra 500.000 donorer under sin 2010-kampagne. Mens nogle kritikere kalder det digital tiggeri, understreger Wales vigtigheden af neutralitet: 'Tænk at læse om General Motors med en Corvette-reklame ved siden af.' Entreprenøren påpeger dog, han ikke er principielt mod reklamer – han driver selv Wikia, en kommerciel platform med over 200.000 fællesskabsskabte spil- og underholdningswikis. Wales sammenligner Wikipedia med 'et sindets tempel', vedligeholdt af frivillige verden over med over 1,7 milliarder redigeringer. 'Det virker umuligt, men det fungerer gennem menneskelig samarbejdslyst,' konstaterede han om den crowdsourced model.

article_content: Residents of Grindavik evacuated as Iceland faces imminent volcanic threat. Authorities declared a state of emergency Saturday, mandating evacuation for the 3,800-person fishing town on Reykjanes peninsula. Recent seismic activity includes 900 earthquakes recorded Monday alone, part of weeks of tremors causing structural damage. Scientists confirm magma movement 5km underground, with land rising 9cm since October 27. The Icelandic Meteorological Office warns of 'significant likelihood' of eruption despite decreasing quake intensity. Evacuees briefly returned Sunday to retrieve essentials, with most finding private accommodation. Historical data shows three recent eruptions (March 2021, August 2022, July 2023) on Reykjanes, with experts predicting decades of activity. Reykjavik remains unaffected 40km (25 miles) northeast.

article_content: Public health officials report respiratory viruses are beginning their seasonal spread, though current transmission levels remain lower than those observed last October. According to CDC's latest monitoring data, influenza-related hospitalizations reached 1,127 cases in early October - a modest increase from the previous week's 1,050 hospitalizations. Southeastern states accounted for 35% of these cases, aligning with typical early-season patterns. The predominant flu strain identified remains Influenza A(H1N1), which matches the variant targeted by this year's vaccine formula. While national respiratory illness metrics stay below baseline levels, Region 9 states (Arizona, California, Hawaii, and Nevada) report increased activity. Alaska currently experiences the nation's only moderate-level respiratory virus transmission. RSV cases continue their expected autumn rise, with surveillance data projecting further increases through winter months. Health experts note this contrasts with last year's 'tripledemic' concerns, as current viral patterns appear more predictable. 'We're seeing textbook seasonal progression now, though healthcare networks remain prepared for potential surges,' observed Dr. John Brownstein of Boston Children's Hospital. Updated vaccines for COVID-19 and influenza are recommended before November, with federal health officials reporting over 7 million administered doses of the new COVID-19 formulation. Specialized RSV protections include vaccines for seniors and late-term pregnant patients, plus the nirsevimab monoclonal antibody treatment providing infants five months' protection against severe infection.

Mens landsdækkende tal for luftvejssygdomme er under normalniveauet, viser Region 9 (Arizona, Californien, Hawaii og Nevada) stigende aktivitet. Alaska har landets eneste område med moderat smitteniveau. RSV-tilfælde stiger som forventet om efteråret, og prognoser viser flere tilfælde i vinter. Dette adskiller sig fra sidste års bekymring om 'tripledemi', da nuværende virustendenser er mere stabile. 'Vi ser nu normal sæsonudvikling, men hospitalerne er klar til eventuelle udbrud,' siger Dr. John Brownstein fra Boston Children's Hospital. Opdaterede COVID-19 og influenza-vacciner anbefales inden november. Over 7 millioner har allerede fået den nye COVID-19-vaccine. article_content: Football fans in Madrid are accustomed to their city attracting top talent. In 2009, Real Madrid—the world's most successful club—invested over $200 million to sign former World Players of the Year Cristiano Ronaldo and Kaká. Now, Madrid's Zoo Aquarium aims to make headlines with an unprecedented offer: a blank-check bid to acquire Paul the octopus, the psychic sea creature who accurately predicted Spain's 2010 World Cup victory. Caretakers emphasized Paul would receive 'hero-level treatment' in Spain. Paul, currently at Germany's Sea Life Center Oberhausen, achieved global fame by correctly predicting all eight World Cup matches—including Spain's final win against the Netherlands and Germany's third-place victory over Uruguay. His method involved choosing between mussel-filled boxes marked with national flags. Though retired from predictions, Paul's team reports receiving worldwide offers. PR expert Max Clifford suggested the octopus could become history's first multimillionaire cephalopod if monetized.

article_content: As part of Hispanic Heritage Month celebrations (Sept 15-Oct 15), World Cafe's '21 Days of Musica Latina' highlights Nicaragua's musical contributions. The country significantly influenced the socially charged nueva canción movement, exemplified by Dúo Guardabarranco's folk-based political commentary during 1980s conflicts. Carlos Mejía Godoy's revolutionary songs became anthems against the Somoza dictatorship. Contemporary artists like electronic producer Rigoazulado, bilingual singer HYRA, and folk artist Ceshia Ubau continue this legacy. The playlist unexpectedly connects to global hits: Nicaraguan percussionist José Areas performed on Santana's 1970 track 'Se a Cabo,' while producer DJ Gordo (born Juan Carlos Cedeno) shaped Drake's 2022 single 'Massive.' This collection bridges historical protest music with modern cross-cultural collaborations.

Carlos Mejía Godoys revolutionære sange blev modstandssymboler mod Somoza-diktaturet. Nutidens kunstnere som den eksperimenterende producer Rigoazulado, den tokulturelle sanger HYRA og folkemusiker Ceshia Ubau fortsætter traditionen. Playlisten viser overraskende globale forbindelser: Nicaraguanske percussionist José Areas medvirkede på Santanas klassiker 'Se a Cabo' (1970), mens produceren DJ Gordo (født Juan Carlos Cedeno) prægede Drakes 2022-hit 'Massive.' article_content: The Senate Judiciary Committee held initial votes on a comprehensive bipartisan immigration bill Thursday, rejecting Republican efforts to expand border security measures. During an eight-hour session, the committee debated over 30 amendments, adopting most without altering core provisions of the 844-page legislation. Sen. Lindsey Graham (R-SC) noted the partisan divide: 'Democrats tend to view the border as secure, while Republicans disagree. This dynamic will shape voting patterns.' Graham and Sen. Jeff Flake (R-AZ), both members of the bipartisan 'Gang of Eight' (4 Democrats, 4 Republicans), aligned with committee Democrats on key votes. Sen. Chuck Schumer (D-NY) urged constructive engagement: 'This bill represents our best chance to break the partisan gridlock that has strangled the Senate, Congress, and the country. Don't make an effort to kill immigration reform.' The committee rejected amendments requiring six months of proven border control before legalization (Sen. Grassley) and proposals to triple Border Patrol agents while quadrupling surveillance equipment (Sen. Cruz), citing fiscal irresponsibility concerns. The legislation proposes new border security resources with effectiveness metrics, alongside a 13-year citizenship pathway for undocumented immigrants. This would be the first major immigration policy overhaul since 1986. Supporters argue it resolves 11 million residents' status; critics call it amnesty. Deliberations resume next Tuesday.

Under et 8-timers maratonmøde drøftede udvalget over 30 ændringsforslag - de fleste blev vedtaget uden ændringer af lovens kerneindhold på 844 sider. Senator Lindsey Graham (R-SC) udpegede den partipolitiske kløft: 'Demokrater vurderer grænsen som sikker, republikanere er uenige. Denne dynamik vil præge afstemningerne.' Graham og Jeff Flake (R-AZ) fra den tvaerpolitiske 'Otte-gruppen' (4 demokrater, 4 republikanere) stemte sammen med demokraterne på afgørende punkter. Chuck Schumer (D-NY) appellerede: 'Denne lov er vores bedste chance for at bryde den politiske deadlock, der har lammet Senatet, Kongressen og landet. Lad vær med at sabotere reformen.' Udvalget afviste krav om 6 måneders dokumenteret grænsekontrol før legalisering (Grassley) og forslag om tredobling af grænsevagter samt firdobling af overvågningsudstyr (Cruz) med henvisning til økonomisk uansvarlighed. Loven indeholder nye grænsesikkerhedsforanstaltninger med effektivitetsmål og en 13-årig vej til statsborgerskab for udokumenterede immigranter - den første store reform siden 1986. Tilhængere hævder den løser status for 11 millioner; modstandere kalder det amnesti. Debatten fortsætter næste tirsdag.

article_content: Tesco's incoming chief executive Dave Lewis has received strategic recommendations to revitalize the struggling supermarket giant. Industry experts suggest dividing operations into three distinct chains: premium 'Finest' outlets, budget-friendly 'Everyday Value' stores, and standard branches. This proposed restructuring aims to better compete with German discount rivals Aldi and Lidl, which have significantly eroded Tesco's market position. Financial pressures mount as Tesco's market valuation plummeted by £10 billion over the past year, with shares dropping 33% to 247p as of August 2014. The retailer faces dual challenges: domestic customers shifting to cheaper alternatives and underperforming international operations, including exits from US and Japanese markets. Analyst Bruno Monteyne argues that maintaining uniform pricing nationwide puts Tesco at a competitive disadvantage, proposing instead localized pricing strategies tailored to regional economic conditions. Recent analysis reveals Lidl's prices are 29.5% lower than Tesco's on comparable baskets, with Aldi showing similar cost advantages. Both discount chains have captured significant market share - Aldi growing 32.2% and Lidl 19.5% in the 12 months to July 2014. Monteyne's blueprint includes streamlining product ranges and adjusting store formats based on neighborhood demographics: 'In affluent areas, emphasize premium offerings; in economically challenged regions, focus on value essentials with cost-efficient operations.' The leadership transition follows Philip Clarke's departure after a £1bn modernization effort - including price reductions, store renovations, and staff expansions - failed to reverse declining fortunes. Industry observers suggest the proposed tri-brand strategy could enable targeted competition while addressing criticisms of Tesco's previous expansion strategies.

Denne omstrukturering skal hjælpe med at konkurrere bedre med de tyske discounters Aldi og Lidl, der har undermineret Tescos position. Økonomisk pres stiger efter Tescos markedsværdi faldt med £10 milliarder på et år, med aktiekursen nede på 247p i august 2014. Udfordringerne er dobbelte: Danske kunder vælger billigere alternativer, mens internationale aktiviteter kæmper - herunder exit fra USA og Japan. Analytiker Bruno Monteyne mener landsdækkende ensprisning sætter Tesco dårligt, og foreslår i stedet lokale priser tilpasset regionalt købekraft. Analyser viser Lidls varer er 29,5% billigere end Tescos på sammenlignelige produkter. Begge discountkæder har vundet markedsandele - Aldi +32,2% og Lidl +19,5% i året op til juli 2014. Monteynes plan indeholder skræddersyede løsninger: 'I velstillede områder skal der investeres i ekspertpersonalet og premiumvarer. I udsatte områder skal fokus være på enkle løsninger med lave omkostninger.' Ledelsesskiftet følger efter at Philip Clarkes £1 milliard investering i prisfald, butiksopdateringer og flere medarbejdere ikke bremsede faldet. Brancheeksperter håber den nye tre-delt strategi kan skabe mere målrettet konkurrenceevne.

article_content: Bernice McTell, a 52-year-old widow from Sheffield, survives on £5 weekly after dedicating her benefits to pet care. Following her husband Kane's death in a 2009 arson attack and her own three-year coma from a stroke at 25, she maintains three dogs, two cats, four birds, and two snakes. 'They give me purpose to endure arthritis pain,' she states, allocating £160 monthly for pet food while subsisting on minimal meals. With £128 weekly benefits, £80 goes to rent/bills and over £40 to pet supplies. Facing the 'bedroom tax' policy change, McTell must forfeit £17 weekly or downsize her home of 16 years - an impossible choice requiring pet abandonment. Her animal companions include Afghan hounds Maverick and Zubin, chihuahua Chico, rescue cats, multiple birds, and snakes. 'I've saved Maverick's life, and he saves mine daily,' McTell reflects, referencing her husband's tragic death and own health battles. 'This unconditional love keeps me going when human judgment fails. They're my irreplaceable family.'

article_content: Recent polling indicates Republicans are positioned to gain control of the Senate, with NBC News/Marist surveys showing GOP leads in crucial battleground states including Colorado, Arkansas, and Iowa. article_content: Fire authorities have released a startling demonstration video showing a mannequin being torn apart by an industrial 'Onion Bomb' firework. The footage, intended as a safety warning ahead of Bonfire Night celebrations, captures the dummy's arm flying off and torso being thrown backward by the explosion's force. This comes after a serious 2022 incident where a 10-year-old Salford boy lost his hair, eyebrows, and eyelashes while suffering facial burns from prohibited pyrotechnics. As part of their annual Treacle safety campaign, Greater Manchester Fire Service published the graphic video on YouTube. Prevention Director Peter O'Reilly emphasized: 'We want families to enjoy festivities safely. This shows the horrific consequences when safety measures are ignored.' The demonstration references a case where a child required hospital treatment including morphine after an Onion Bomb exploded in his hands. Authorities are conducting compliance checks on firework sellers until November 10. Assistant Chief Constable Garry Shewan warned: 'We'll take action against fireworks-related antisocial behavior.' article_content: (CNN) -- Strikes between Israel and Hamas resumed after negotiations for a prolonged ceasefire collapsed. Since Tuesday's truce breakdown, the Israeli military reports at least 137 rockets launched from Gaza, with 94 reaching Israeli territory and 24 intercepted. Air raid sirens sounded repeatedly in the Eshkol region, Ashdod, and other areas Wednesday. One rocket struck a home in Ashkelon without causing injuries. Israeli airstrikes targeted approximately 80 suspected militant sites in Gaza, resulting in 23 deaths and over 130 injuries according to Gaza's Health Ministry (which operates under Hamas administration). While Hamas claims an attack targeted Qassam Brigades leader Mohammed Deif, the ministry reported his wife and 7-month-old son were killed. Hamas official Mousa Marzhouk stated Deif remains alive and 'in a safe place,' with Israeli forces investigating the claim. Hamas spokesman Sami Abu Zuhri warned Israel would 'pay a heavy price' for 'crimes against civilians,' asserting conflict resolution depends on Deif's decisions and Israel ending its blockade. The Qassam Brigades (Hamas' military wing) issued a warning to international airlines regarding Ben Gurion Airport operations starting Thursday. Both sides blamed each other for the ceasefire's collapse. Israel resumed strikes after three rockets were fired from Gaza, which Hamas denied launching. Negotiations faltered over Israel's demilitarization demands versus Palestinian calls to lift the blockade. Hamas negotiator Izzat Risheq accused Israel of bad-faith negotiations, while Israel maintains security concerns prevent easing restrictions while militants arm themselves. PLO's Saeb Erekat accused Israeli PM Netanyahu of sabotaging peace efforts, warning of 'worse to come.' Netanyahu countered: 'Our policy is simple: If you shoot, you will get attacked.' The conflict has left over 2,000 Palestinians and 67 Israelis dead since July, with extensive damage in Gaza neighborhoods.

article_content: Rock legend Eric Clapton's ultra-rare platinum Patek Philippe watch is set to sell for up to £2.6 million at Christie's Geneva auction on November 12, 2012. Only two such platinum models exist, with the other housed in a museum. This 1951 timepiece, first sold in 1989, headlines a collection of 310 luxury watches valued at $16 million. The auction follows Clapton's October 2012 sale of a Gerhard Richter painting for £21.3 million at Sotheby's London, a record for a living artist. The guitarist purchased the artwork for £2 million in 2001. Clapton, who studied art before his music career, has built a significant collection with his £140 million fortune. Also featured is the Archduke Joseph Diamond, a 76-carat internally flawless stone from India's Golconda mines. Estimated at $25 million, it previously belonged to Austria's Habsburg royal family until the 1930s.

article_content: A federal judge ruled Thursday that a lawsuit alleging torture and abuse of Iraqi detainees by civilian interrogators at Abu Ghraib prison can proceed. U.S. District Court Judge Gerald Bruce Lee rejected defense contractor CACI's legal argument claiming immunity from allegations of physical abuse, war crimes, and civil conspiracy. The case involves four Iraqi detainees released between 2004-2008 without criminal charges. Court documents allege contract interrogators at Baghdad Central Prison (Abu Ghraib) engaged in beatings, psychological torture, evidence destruction, and providing false information to authorities. While 11 U.S. soldiers were court-martialed under military law for prisoner abuse, civilian contractors have not faced criminal prosecution. CACI maintains its actions constituted government-contracted services, arguing the case involves political questions beyond civilian court jurisdiction. Judge Lee ruled that judicial review serves public accountability interests. Katherine Gallagher of the Center for Constitutional Rights emphasized: 'Military contractors must comply with international and U.S. laws. Accountability for Abu Ghraib atrocities remains crucial.' The pending case (Al Shimari v. CACI Premier Technology Inc., 1:08cv827) may establish legal standards for contractor liability in conflict zones.

Sagen omhandler fire tidligere fanger fra Abu Ghraib, løsladt mellem 2004-2008 uden tiltale. Ifølge retsdokumenter skulle civile kontraktansatte have udsat dem for vold, psykisk tortur og bevisfjernelse, samt vildledt myndigheder. Mens 11 soldater er dømt ved krigsret, er ingen civile entreprenører straffet. CACI argumenterer, at deres handlinger var statsanordnede, men dommeren fastslog at retten bør vurdere ansvar uden politisk indblanding. Katherine Gallagher fra Center for Constitutional Rights udtalte: 'Privatkrigere må holdes ansvarlige efter loven. Abu Ghraib-overgrebene kræver retfærdighed.' Den igangæværende sag (Al Shimari mod CACI, 1:08cv827) kan blive en mærkesag for entreprenøransvar i krigszoner.

article_content: NASA postponed space shuttle Discovery's Florida landing Friday due to unstable weather at Kennedy Space Center. Mission Control canceled two landing attempts as forecasts predicted persistent thunderstorms and lightning risks. The shuttle will complete another Earth orbit while awaiting improved conditions. Edwards Air Force Base in California remains on standby with clear weather, offering two Friday evening landing opportunities. NASA typically prioritizes Florida landings to avoid additional logistical costs - a West Coast touchdown requires substantial extra expenses and adds a week to mission turnaround. Discovery's crew concluded a 13-day International Space Station mission featuring three spacewalks, equipment repairs, and delivery of supplies including the COLBERT treadmill named after comedian Stephen Colbert. The mission faced three launch delays before its eventual departure.

article_content: Climate disasters now cost the United States billions annually, with impacts disproportionately affecting vulnerable populations, according to the latest National Climate Assessment. Published every four years, this fifth edition marks the first inclusion of dedicated chapters analyzing economic consequences and social inequities. Intensifying floods, wildfires, heatwaves, and other climate-driven catastrophes are imposing mounting financial burdens while exacerbating environmental injustices. The report notes current global temperature increases surpass any recorded in two millennia, creating unprecedented risks. Examples include the lethal 2021 Pacific Northwest heatwave and the Southwest's most severe drought in 1,200 years. Economic impacts extend beyond immediate disaster costs. Since 1980, droughts and heatwaves alone caused over $320 billion in damages. Billion-dollar disasters now strike monthly rather than quarterly. Annual losses exceed $150 billion, excluding healthcare costs and ecological damage. Climate change permeates daily economics through food price increases and threatened agricultural stability. Midwestern corn and apple harvests face climate-stressed pests and erratic weather, while Alaska's fisheries suffer collapse - particularly impacting Indigenous communities. Marginalization compounds climate risks: Census tracts with ≥20% Black residents face flood damage rates doubling those with <1% Black residents, a legacy of racist housing policies. Formerly redlined neighborhoods endure 12°F higher temperatures due to urban heat island effects. Despite being the top fossil fuel producer, US climate progress remains inadequate. Annual emissions reductions of 1% since 2005 fall far short of the 6% needed to meet Paris Agreement targets. At current trajectories, 2°C warming would double economic losses.

Femte udgave af den fjerneårige rapport inkluderer første gang dybdegående analyser af økonomiske konsekvenser og social ulighed. Eskalerende oversvømmelser, skovbrande, hedebølger og andre klimadrevne katastrofer øger både finansielle omkostninger og miljømæssig uretfærdighed. Rapporten konkluderer, at nuværende temperaturstigninger overgår alle mål i de seneste 2.000 år. Blandt eksemplerne er den dødelige hedebølge i Pacific Northwest 2021 og Sydvestens værste tørke i 1.200 år. Økonomiske virkninger strækker sig langt ud over akutte skader. Siden 1980 har tørker og hedebølger alene forårsaget over 320 milliarder dollars i tab. Milliardkatastrofer indtræffer nu hver måned i stedet for hver fjerde måned. Årlige tab overstiger 150 milliarder dollar, uden at medregne sundhedsomkostninger eller økosystemskader. Klimakrisen påvirker hverdagsøkonomien gennem stigende fødevarepriser og truede landbrugssektorer. Midtvestens majs- og æbleproduktion rammes af klimaforværrede skadedyr og uforudsigeligt vejr, mens Alaskas fiskerier kollapser - især med alvorlige konsekvenser for oprindelige folkegrupper. Social marginalisering forstærker klimarisici: Områder med mindst 20% sorte indbyggere oplever dobbelt så hurtig stigning i oversvømmelsesskader sammenlignet med områder under 1% - en arv fra historisk racistisk boligpolitik. Tidligere 'redlined' kvarterer er 12°F (6.7°C) varmere grundet manglende grønne områder og asfalts overflader. Trods status som verdens største olie- og gasproducent, er USAs klimatiltag utilstrækkelige. Årlige CO2-reduktioner på 1% siden 2005 når langt ikke de 6% krævet for Paris-aftalens mål. Ved nuværende udledning vil 2°C opvarmning fordoble de økonomiske tab.

article_content: The Edinburgh International Festival has unveiled its 2024 programme under director Nicola Benedetti, featuring the theme 'Rituals That Unite Us'. Building on 2023's 'Where Do We Go From Here?', this edition emphasizes shared experiences in a disconnected world through opera, theatre, and dance. Five opera productions will headline, including a special Carmen revival by Paris's Opéra-Comique - performed on a replica of its original 1875 stage featuring seven iron doors created by Gustave Eiffel. The festival will also showcase Canadian choreographer Crystal Pate's Assembly Hall, a medieval re-enactment narrative making its Scottish debut. Community initiatives include the Healing Arts Scotland campaign with WHO and Scottish Ballet, continuing last year's success of mass participatory events like the 500-musician Princes Street Gardens performance.

Fem operaopsætninger inkluderer en speciel Carmen-genopførelse fra Paris' Opéra-Comique - opført på en replika af den originale 1875-scene med syv jernporte designet af Gustave Eiffel. Festivalen præsenterer også canadiske koreograf Crystal Pates 'Assembly Hall', en fortælling om middelalder-genopførelser med skotsk premiere. article_content: Manchester United captain Wayne Rooney praised his team's strategic approach following their 2-1 victory over Arsenal at Emirates Stadium on Saturday. Rooney scored United's second goal after an own goal by Kieran Gibbs opened the scoring, marking manager Louis van Gaal's first away win with the club. 'This victory holds significant importance,' Rooney told Sky Sports. 'We maintained defensive resilience, particularly in the first half, and capitalized on counter-attacking opportunities. While Arsenal controlled possession, our tactical adjustments proved effective. Goalkeeper David de Gea delivered crucial saves, and our two well-executed goals made the difference.' Despite fielding an inexperienced defensive lineup featuring Paddy McNair and Tyler Blackett, Rooney commended their composure: 'These young players handled the pressure exceptionally well. This performance should boost our confidence as we approach upcoming matches.' The captain added: 'We're focusing on incremental progress following our inconsistent start. Securing six points from the next two home games could establish valuable momentum heading into the new year.'

article_content: A court has ordered the euthanasia of Diesel, a Japanese Akita deemed 'exceptionally dangerous' by West Midlands Police, following a May 2022 attack on 9-year-old Amy Hryhoruk in Rushall. The dog escaped its owner's property and inflicted severe head injuries requiring 20 stitches, while Amy's father Simon sustained bite wounds necessitating two surgeries during rescue efforts. Nirmal Singh, overseeing the dog during the incident, received a £750 fine and was ordered to pay £7,653.81 in kennel costs plus £1,200 court fees. Judge Michael Walsh affirmed the destruction order, stating Diesel presented 'significant public risk.' PC Keith Evans, a police dog specialist, described this as one of the most severe attacks he'd witnessed. The Hryhoruk family expressed relief at the court's decision while advocating for legal reforms regarding owner liability. Amy's grandfather emphasized current laws' limitations when owners aren't present during attacks.

Nirmal Singh, der havde ansvaret for hunden under angrebet, blev idømt en bøde på 750 pund samt pålagt at betale 7.653,81 pund i hundepensionsomkostninger og 1.200 pund i retsgebyrer. Dommer Michael Walsh fastslog at aflivning var nødvendig grundet 'betydelig fare for offentligheden'. Polititjenestemand Keith Evans beskrev episoden som et af de værste hundeangreb i sin karriere. article_content: Guinean authorities report armed thieves intercepted a shipment of Ebola-contaminated blood samples en route to a testing facility. The incident occurred near Kissidougou, where four Red Cross personnel were transporting the biological material in sealed containers. Officials suspect the perpetrators mistakenly believed the shipment contained valuables rather than hazardous medical samples. Health authorities issued urgent appeals via national radio for the safe return of the stolen specimens, originally collected from an Ebola patient. This security breach highlights ongoing challenges in epidemic response logistics, despite substantial international aid to West African nations combating the virus responsible for over 5,400 fatalities. Faya Etienne Tolno of Guinea's Red Cross explained the organization's reliance on civilian transport due to vehicle shortages. 'We're perplexed by this theft – perhaps they thought cash was stored in the thermal flask,' Tolno stated. Dr. Barry Moumie, overseeing national Ebola response, warned of contamination risks and pledged enhanced security measures for future medical transports. In parallel developments, WHO announced the conclusion of Congo's Ebola outbreak after 42 days without new cases, contrasting with West Africa's ongoing crisis. Meanwhile, a Cuban physician infected in Sierra Leone received specialized treatment in Switzerland, part of Havana's 165-member medical contingent deployed regionally.

Samtidig modtog en cubansk læge smittet i Sierra Leone specialbehandling i Schweiz, som del af Cubas 165-personers medicinteam udsendt i regionen.

article_content: Queen Elizabeth II has accepted a special Diamond Jubilee gift of 97 original artworks from prominent Royal Academy members, including David Hockney and Tracey Emin. The collection features diverse mediums ranging from iPad-generated pieces to traditional drawings, with Hockney's contributions alone carrying significant historical value - his 'Beverly Hills Housewife' sold for £5.2 million in 2009. Rather than keeping these works privately, the Queen has entrusted them to the Royal Collection for public enjoyment. Starting autumn 2013, visitors to Buckingham Palace's Queen's Gallery can view the exhibition, which includes Emin's minimalist monarch portrait and Hockney's digital creation commemorating the 60-year reign. Royal Academy officials emphasized the cultural significance of this gift, noting the institution's 250+ year history dating back to George III's 1768 foundation. The collection showcases both contemporary innovations like Anish Kapoor's abstract red sphere and traditional elements such as John Maine's Westminster Abbey crayon drawing depicting the coronation site.

article_content: A historic 1929 Rolls-Royce Phantom II Sedanca de Ville previously owned by Lord Louis Mountbatten will be auctioned in Denmark on Sunday, starting at £50,000. The battleship grey automobile retains Mountbatten's original British registration plate LM3698 and honors his naval service through its color scheme. Featuring coachwork by renowned builder Barker & Co., this 7.7-liter six-cylinder luxury vehicle was delivered new to Mountbatten in February 1930. Its design includes an exposed front compartment for chauffeurs and enclosed rear seating for passengers. Part of the Aalholm Automobil Museum's collection until its 2007 closure, the Phantom II remains in working condition with minor cosmetic flaws noted by auctioneers RM Auctions. The car's historical significance is enhanced by Mountbatten's roles as last Viceroy of India and Supreme Allied Commander in Southeast Asia during WWII. Lord Mountbatten's 1979 assassination by the IRA and his status as Queen Elizabeth II's second cousin contribute to the vehicle's provenance. The auction includes nearly 100 cars from the Danish museum's collection.

Med karosseri fra legendariske Barker & Co. og en 7,7-liters sekscylindret motor blev denne luksusvogn leveret til Mountbatten i februar 1930. Designet inkluderer et åbent førerrum til chaufføren og lukket kabine til passagererne. article_content: When Deborah Lee James became Air Force Secretary in December 2013, she didn't anticipate a nuclear crisis. After discovering exam cheating by missile officers, she publicly acknowledged systemic issues others had avoided addressing. James concluded the nuclear corps faced deep-rooted problems including 'spotty' morale requiring urgent reforms. Following January 2014 visits to three ICBM bases, James told the Associated Press: 'I recognized cultural issues beyond cheating. We needed comprehensive solutions.' Her direct approach contrasted with previous leaders' reluctance to acknowledge problems publicly. Congressional leaders praised her transparency. Rep. Howard McKeon noted: 'She addressed leadership failures differently than past administrations.' James, the second female Air Force Secretary, initiated reforms after AP's 2013 reports revealed nuclear force issues, including 19 Minot Base officers being sidelined for performance failures. Despite initial military claims that problems were 'localized,' James found widespread concerns during base visits. Airmen questioned why critical missile infrastructure remained underfunded despite nuclear missions being labeled top priority. 'Some issues were longstanding,' James admitted, questioning why previous leaders hadn't acted. With prior experience on the House Armed Services Committee and defense contracting, James applied her expertise to implement reforms. Colleague John Hamre noted: 'She tackled the ICBM crisis directly rather than minimizing it.' James summarized her approach: 'You must confront challenges head-on rather than avoid them.'

article_content: Congressional scrutiny of the U.S. Secret Service has escalated following misconduct allegations during presidential security preparations in Colombia. The Homeland Security Committee, chaired by Sen. Joe Lieberman, seeks to determine if the Cartagena incident reflects isolated misconduct or deeper organizational issues. Twelve agency personnel have been implicated, with six resignations confirmed. While maintaining confidence in Director Mark Sullivan's leadership, lawmakers demand thorough accountability. 'Our investigation will establish precise timelines and evaluate potential security breaches,' Lieberman told Fox News. Separate military probes examine 11 service members' alleged involvement in similar activities. Discussions about agency composition emerged, with several legislators advocating for increased gender diversity. Rep. Carolyn Maloney noted women comprise 11% of Secret Service agents, suggesting balanced staffing could enhance operational integrity. White House officials remain unaffected by the ongoing investigations.

article_content: (CNN) -- While President Obama maintains his position against deploying US combat troops in Iraq and Syria, Vice President Joe Biden has indicated potential flexibility depending on operational needs. During a Wednesday event in Des Moines, Iowa with the 'Nuns on the Bus' activist group, Biden stated that ground troop deployment would be assessed 'based on how the effort progresses' against ISIS, according to press reports. This follows White House Press Secretary Josh Earnest's earlier reaffirmation of Obama's stance: 'The President will not consider options involving American military personnel in ground combat roles.' Obama previously emphasized in a national address that combating ISIS 'will not involve American combat troops fighting on foreign soil.' However, Gen. Martin Dempsey, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, introduced complexity during a Senate hearing by stating he would recommend US troops accompany Iraqi forces against specific ISIL targets if necessary. Biden addressed this discrepancy, noting Dempsey 'would request presidential approval if needed, but currently deems it unnecessary.' CNN's David Chalian contributed reporting.

Under en begivenhed i Des Moines, Iowa onsdag med aktivistgruppen 'Nuns on the Bus' udtalte Biden ifølge medierne, at udsendelse af jordtropper vil blive vurderet 'baseret på indsatsens udvikling' mod ISIS. Dette følger efter at White Houses pressesekretær Josh Earnest tidligere bekræftede Obamas holdning: 'Præsidenten vil ikke overveje muligheder med amerikanske soldater i jordbaserede kamproller.' Obama understregede tidligere i en national tale, at ISIS-bekæmpelsen 'ikke vil involvere amerikanske kampstyrker i kamphandlinger på udenlandsk jord.' General Martin Dempsey, formand for Forsvarscheferne, tilføjede kompleksitet under et senatsmøde ved at sige, han ville anbefale amerikanske styrker som støtte til irakiske enheder mod specifikke ISIL-mål hvis nødvendigt. article_content: North Dakota maintains the nation's highest density of drinking establishments, with one bar serving every 1,621 residents according to 2011 Census data. The state narrowly surpasses Montana in this metric, while Virginia reports the lowest ratio nationally with just 125 bars for 8 million people. Community leaders and health officials cite multiple contributing factors. 'In our small towns, bars function as central gathering places - they're where residents connect over meals and drinks,' notes Jason Stein of Davenport's Supper Club. Pam Sagness from the state health department observes that North Dakota's cultural acceptance of heavy drinking, combined with limited entertainment alternatives in rural areas, perpetuates alcohol-related issues. The decentralized alcohol regulation system, managed by local governments rather than state agencies, further influences accessibility. While bar owners emphasize their establishments' social role, public health experts warn this environment exacerbates North Dakota's chronic problems with binge drinking and impaired driving.

Lokale eksperter forklarer fænomenet med tynd befolkning og få fritidstilbud på landet. 'I små samfund er baren det sociale centrum - her mødes folk til mad, drikke og hygge,' siger Jason Schmidt, der driver Supper Club i Davenport. Sundhedsekspert Pam Sagness peger på, at den lokale 'arbejd hårdt, fest hårdt'-mentalitet normaliserer et stort alkoholforbrug, der har udviklet sig over generationer. Den manglende landsdækkende alkoholregulering, hvor kommunerne styrer udstedelse af spirituslicenser, spiller også ind. Mens branchen understreger barernes samfundsrolle, advarer sundhedsmyndigheder om, at den lette adgang forværrer Norddakotas problemer med binge-drinking og spiritusrelaterede trafikuheld.

article_content: By Daniel Miller. Hundreds of thousands of unsold tickets for Olympic events, including the opening ceremony and swimming finals, are reportedly being offered to corporate sponsors through an internal system, despite prior commitments to make them available to the public. The tickets consist of unsold allocations returned by foreign Olympic committees. London 2012 Chairman Lord Coe had previously urged committees to return unwanted tickets to meet 'phenomenal and unprecedented' public demand. However, Locog began distributing these returned tickets to sponsors and officials 12 days ago without public access. article_content: A Welsh motorist reported significant vehicle damage when his vaping device unexpectedly exploded during charging. Chris Thomas (37) from Maesycwmmer described the incident occurring overnight in his company-owned Skoda Superb, where the Vapouriz Tank e-cigarette discharged 'like pyrotechnics' from the 12V socket, igniting interior materials. The resulting blaze destroyed rear seating, a child seat, and caused extensive smoke damage throughout the cabin. The automotive technician, who switched to vaping four months ago to quit his 40-cigarette daily habit, stated he discovered the damage after silencing a car alarm earlier that night. 'I returned to bed thinking nothing was wrong, only to find the interior completely charred hours later,' Thomas recounted. 'The £29.99 device had been charging upfront - it's terrifying to imagine this happening in a home or with children present.' Vapouriz, the device manufacturer, noted Thomas hadn't formally reported the incident but suggested improper charger use might be responsible. Their spokesperson emphasized: 'Our products use non-flammable e-liquids when properly diluted. We explicitly warn against unattended charging.' The company confirmed Thomas recently purchased e-liquid but not replacement hardware. This case follows similar international incidents, including a Utah toddler injured by an exploding device last week. While promoted as smoking cessation aids, recent studies highlight ongoing safety debates around lithium-ion batteries in vaping equipment. Over 5 million users across the UK and US now utilize these devices, with major tobacco companies increasingly entering the market amid growing regulatory scrutiny.

article_content: NAIROBI: Kenya risks losing up to 7% of its economic output by 2050 due to climate change without adaptation measures, according to a World Bank report released Friday. The East African nation—already reeling from prolonged drought and recent El Niño-induced floods—faces heightened vulnerability to climate disasters. The report warns that unaddressed climate impacts could increase poverty by 1.1 million people and escalate malaria cases by 56% and waterborne diseases by 10% by mid-century. However, fiscal constraints complicate these efforts. With public debt at 10.1 trillion shillings ($66 billion)—equivalent to two-thirds of GDP—and a $2 billion eurobond repayment due in 2024, Kenya struggles to balance climate priorities against economic stabilization. The agriculture sector, contributing 21% to GDP in 2022, remains particularly exposed to extreme weather patterns.

article_content: Researchers at California's National Ignition Facility achieved an unprecedented energy milestone on March 15, 2012. Their 192-laser system generated a 411-trillion-watt pulse lasting 23 billionths of a second - equivalent to 1,000 times the nation's peak electricity demand. This test advances efforts to achieve controlled nuclear fusion by compressing hydrogen isotopes to extreme densities, mimicking stellar energy production. While not yet targeting fuel capsules, the experiment marks crucial progress toward ignition - the threshold where fusion becomes self-sustaining. NIF Director Edward Moses likened this achievement to breaking a 'scientific sound barrier.' The process involves fusing deuterium and tritium atoms into helium, harnessing released neutrons to potentially drive power generation systems. The project faces scrutiny due to its weapons research connections and environmental concerns. Critics argue investment should focus on existing renewables rather than fusion's unproven scalability, despite its clean energy potential.

Familien håber nu på at samle nok penge ind til en anden bionisk hånd, der kan monteres, når Alan bliver 12.
